expectations.text: A1: Parses the untrusted body with safeParse (NOT parse)
expectations.evidence: `const result = signupSchema.safeParse(request.body)` with branch on `!result.success`; no `.parse()`.

expectations.text: A2: Coerces the form-string age to a number (z.coerce.number / z.preprocess) rather than z.number() on a string
expectations.evidence: `age: z.coerce.number({...}).int().min(18).max(120)` with note that z.coerce.number runs Number() before validating.

expectations.text: A3: Models role as z.enum([...]) not a plain z.string()
expectations.evidence: `role: z.enum(['admin', 'editor', 'viewer'], {...})` with note 'Do not use z.string() plus a manual check'.

expectations.text: A4: Validates email with .email() at the schema
expectations.evidence: `.email('Please enter a valid email address.')` chained on the email string schema.

expectations.text: A5: Derives the TS type via z.infer, not a hand-written interface
expectations.evidence: `export type SignupInput = z.infer<typeof signupSchema>` with note 'Infer the type from the schema so it can never drift'.

expectations.text: A6: Returns field-by-field errors via flatten() (or path-keyed issues), not a raw ZodError dump
expectations.evidence: `const { fieldErrors, formErrors } = result.error.flatten()`; example JSON shows per-field messages.

expectations.text: A7: Models bio with .optional() (and handles optional-vs-nullable correctly)
expectations.evidence: `bio: z.string().trim().max(500).optional()` and explicit 'Use .optional() (not .nullable()) because an absent form field is undefined, not null'.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline hit all 7 assertions cleanly. Difference vs with_skill is presentation only (no repo version pinning, no rule citations); every checked outcome is present.
